Fix what the output names. Move the tasks it touches to in_progress with UpdateTask while you work and to tested once their tests pass; leave the rest of the board as it is.

Reproduce the failure with a run narrowed to the test the output names, fix it, then run that test again and build its project. The whole sweep runs again as soon as you stop with every task tested, so stopping on a fix you have not run costs another one.

CodeOutline on the failing test's file gives the line each test starts on: Read that test's range rather than the whole file.

The tasks the failure names:

Rules that became optional [tested] (Core behaviour stays in the prompt, Optional mechanics ship as bundles, The agent's own style stays core, Not pre-applied on upgrade, Bundle rules reach a session as the person's own instructions do, Person-scope bundle on either engine, Clash with a core rule, No bundles for the blind planner): What the agent guarantees about itself and what the person chooses are no longer the same list.

proves: Core behaviour stays in the prompt → test/instruction-files-session.test.ts core behaviour stays in the prompt > joining the instruction files never drops or rewrites the phase's own prompt, Optional mechanics ship as bundles → test/instruction-files-session.test.ts optional mechanics ship as bundles > a rule from an instruction file reaches the session only as the appended text of that file, never folded into the phase prompt itself, The agent's own style stays core → test/system-prompt.test.ts buildSystemPrompt > the agent's own style stays core: an instruction file cannot remove the chat's own rule for how it writes code, Not pre-applied on upgrade → test/instruction-files-session.test.ts not pre-applied on upgrade > a workspace with ordinary instructions and no bundle block carries exactly what is on disk, nothing extra, Bundle rules reach a session as the person's own instructions do → test/mode-setup.test.ts modeSetup > bundle rules reach a session as the person's own instructions do: %s, Person-scope bundle on either engine → test/instruction-files-session.test.ts person-scope bundle on either engine > the person's own instruction file joins a session the same way regardless of which engine reads the resulting text, Clash with a core rule → test/instruction-files-session.test.ts clash with a core rule > the session is told that a rule already given always wins over one an instruction file adds, and to say which it set aside, No bundles for the blind planner → test/mode-setup.test.ts modeSetup > no bundles for the blind planner
note: The context named only implement.ts among the phase files; inspecting every phase prompt (blind-plan, reconcile, cleanup, docs-evaluation, file-decisions, code-plan, docs-map) found no hardcoded judgment/practice rule to extract into a bundle — "Optional mechanics ship as bundles" is delivered by there being no built-in judgment rule left standing and by instruction files (where a later task's applied bundles will live) being the only way such a rule can now reach a session. Asked the user whether system-prompt.ts's "Make the smallest change..." line (the one practice-sounding candidate in the named context) should be stripped as optional; they said it is this agent's own style, not a team's practice, so it stays core — recorded as the edge case "The agent's own style stays core" under that rule in the spec. Claude's own engine auto-reads only the workspace's CLAUDE.md (not AGENTS.md, not the person's), so joining instruction files explicitly for the Claude chat prompt means that one file's text can now appear twice (once via Claude's own preset, once via the explicit join); left as is rather than special-casing one path, since the spec does not ask for deduplication and the duplication is harmless. Second sweep fix: the whole-suite failure was neither test nor source code of this feature — all 123 files failed before their first test ("Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'config')", "Vitest failed to find the runner"), the flake of spawning 120+ child processes on this machine. Neither per-file forks (the vitest default, the previous fix) nor `isolate: false` (the fix before that) is stable; vitest.config.mts now pins `pool: 'threads'`, which keeps per-file isolation but spawns worker threads instead of processes. All 123 files pass, three full runs in a row (~9s each, faster than forks' ~15s), plus a green `npm run typecheck`.
built: `withInstructionFiles(mode, systemPrompt, cwd, home)`, `instructionsText(files)`, `CLASH_WITH_CORE` and `wantsInstructions(mode)` in src/agent/instructions/instruction-files.ts: the one join point where the workspace's and the person's instruction files (and applied bundles) reach a session's prompt, for every mode but the blind planner, with a note telling the model a rule already given always wins and to say which instruction-file rule it set aside. `ModeContext.withInstructions` (src/agent/session/mode-setup.ts) wires it into every non-chat, non-plan mode, wrapped outermost in session-engines.ts's `modeContext()`. The chat prompt on both engines (buildSystemPrompt and session-engines.ts's startClaude) also joins instruction files through the same `instructionsText`/`CLASH_WITH_CORE`. `MemorySources`/`memorySection`/`withMemories`/`chatMemorySection` in src/agent/memory/session-context.ts carry the project's index only; the person's own notes ride the instruction files. Test harness: vitest.config.mts pins `pool: 'threads'` (per-file isolation, thread workers) — the suite is unstable with forks at this file count, so leave that pin in place.

Picking up bundles for a workspace [tested] (Suggested once per workspace, Matched by what the workspace holds, Text seen before it is applied, Project or person scope, One marked block per bundle, Managed at any time): The person has a workspace with no bundles applied, and the agent offers what fits it.

context: src/settings/settings-store.ts, src/settings/protocol.ts, src/settings/webview/profiles-tab.ts, src/settings/webview/providers-tab.ts, src/settings/webview/memories-tab.ts, src/agent/instructions/instruction-files.ts, src/agent/memory/memories.ts
proves: Suggested once per workspace → test/settings-store.test.ts the_offer_is_pending_for_a_workspace_with_nothing_applied_and_a_matching_bundle_not_yet_dismissed / the_offer_is_not_pending_once_dismissed, Matched by what the workspace holds → test/bundles.test.ts matching_the_catalog_always_keeps_the_ones_that_apply_to_nothing_in_particular, Text seen before it is applied → test/settings-app.test.ts a_bundles_rule_text_is_hidden_until_shown_and_only_then_readable_before_it_is_applied, Project or person scope → test/bundles.test.ts a_bundle_applied_for_the_project_lands_in_the_workspaces_agents_md, One marked block per bundle → test/bundles.test.ts removing_a_bundle_drops_only_its_own_block_and_leaves_the_rest_of_the_file, Managed at any time → test/settings-app.test.ts available_and_applied_bundles_can_be_seen_and_managed_without_an_offer_pending
note: The spec is silent on the catalog's own transport (that's "Where bundles come from"), on the block's on-file markup, and on which language/framework names a bundle target may use, so this task's choices: (1) `BundleCatalogPort.available()` as the seam the next task fills with real git sources — wired in extension.ts returning an empty catalog for now; `matching()` already composes it with `workspaceSignals()` correctly. (2) A bundle's block is marked by HTML comments naming source/name/version (`<!-- bundle source="..." name="..." version="..." -->` ... `<!-- /bundle -->`), chosen because AGENTS.md is read as plain text by both engines and a comment reads as ordinary text to a model, same as it would to a person. (3) A language tag is 'csharp', 'typescript' or 'javascript' (the extensions the repo map already recognises); a framework tag is exactly a package.json dependency name or a .csproj PackageReference Include name, so a bundle author names a framework the same way the workspace's own manifest does, with nothing hardcoded in between. (4) The suggestion banner and the full catalog/applied lists live together in one new Settings "Bundles" tab rather than a separate proactive notification, consistent with "Managed at any time" putting both in the same place.
built: src/agent/instructions/bundles.ts: `Bundle`, `BundleScope`, `BundleTarget`, `AppliedBundle`, `BundleCatalogPort`, `WorkspaceSignals`; `bundleFilePath(scope, cwd, home)` (project → `<cwd>/AGENTS.md`, user → `<home>/AGENTS.md`, never CLAUDE.md); the marked-block mechanics `applyBundleText`, `removeBundleText`, `parseAppliedBundles`; the file-backed `appliedBundles`, `applyBundle`, `removeBundle`; the workspace probe `workspaceSignals` (languages from source/project file extensions the repo map already walks, frameworks from package.json dependencies and .csproj PackageReferences) and `bundleMatches`/`matchingBundles`. src/settings/settings-store.ts: `BundlePort` (available/matching/applied/apply/remove, closed over a workspace the same way `MemoryPort` is), `SettingsStore.applyBundle/removeBundle/dismissBundleOffer`, `SettingsSnapshot.bundles` (available, applied, suggested, offerPending) computed from `bundleOfferDismissed` plus the port. src/settings/webview/bundles-tab.ts: `BundlesTab` custom element, the 'bundles' SettingsTab, and events `BundleAppliedEvent`/`BundleRemovedEvent`/`BundleOfferDismissedEvent` in events.ts, wired in settings-app.ts and settings-panel.ts. The `BundlePort` wired in extension.ts has `available()` stubbed to an empty catalog; `matching()`, `applied()`, `apply()`, `remove()` are already real, so the next feature only has to replace `available()` with real git sources.

What earlier tasks left:
